name: Luxury Editorial
visualIdentity: Explicitly described direction: highlight one subject with refined display type, concise copy, generous space, selective image cropping, and restrained color. Material highlights are used sparingly. Luxury must not be equated with excessive gold, sparkle, or blur.
suitableUses: Explicit compatibility lists product and editorial introductions, explanatory and illustrated narratives, and abstract or cinematic sequences with meaningful chapters. Suggested pairings cite fashion, hospitality, invitations, premium reveals, lookbooks, property showcases, and collection launches. These pairing uses are inferred suitability rather than explicit source claims.
limitations: Strongest when used alone with one subject and refined type. Hybridize only to add a tactile title surface or measured depth on cropped imagery. Adapt or omit it when the topic is too short for chapters, when transitions obscure causality, or when a cut violates a continuous-shot or loop requirement. Cropping does not remove backgrounds or create cutouts.
palette: Suggested, not supplied: background #F4EFE7 (ivory), foreground #29251F (dark brown), accent_1 #817159 (muted taupe). Task-supplied exact colors override these and must keep their values and roles. Foreground-on-background contrast is 13.308:1. Accent on background is 4.132:1, which fails normal text and is decorative only. Gradients are disabled; use discrete tokens and never recolor assets.
motionAndInteraction: Motion favors smooth camera moves, subtle parallax, and precise settling. Easing is not required on every transition; deliberate cuts, impacts, and reading holds stay intact. Primary motion owner is a paused GSAP timeline with one owner per animated property. Motion is an optional DOM or SVG layer. Video is driven by composition time, while scroll or pointer input belongs only to interactive delivery.
audio: The source leaves audio unspecified and treats it as a task-driven choice. No music genre, tempo, voice, or mandatory layer is assigned. Explicit user audio requirements take priority. Restrained sound accents, ambience, or silence during reading holds are plausible inferred options. Speech must remain intelligible, and final audio balance, clipping, and picture sync must be verified.
assetRequirements: Requires supplied or authorized imagery and exact copy; the source does not assume photographic assets exist. Use loaded local fonts, image masks, and measured spacing. Optional Cropper.js 2.x crops should preserve originals and store a crop recipe. Render material details separately when needed. Gallery motion needs actual images and captions, and authored illustrations must be clearly labeled.
combinations: Optional supporting style-052 provides letterpress title cards with ink #29251F, #817159 for one rule or monogram, shallow single-direction deboss, and title moments only. Optional style-101 adds slow parallax across cropped layers with one camera move per scene, no generated fill, and no extra grading. Avoid metallic bevels, glitter, gold gradients, and heavy depth blur.
productionApproach: HyperFrames is the default pipeline for scene assembly, timing, sync, validation, and export. Use data-composition-id, a paused GSAP timeline registered in window.__timelines, then check, snapshot, and render. Remotion is a fallback only when its documented condition is met, with the reason recorded. HTML/CSS and SVG handle visuals, and chroma-js validates colors. Verify key frames, audio sync, and loop continuity.
